approaches.name: A: Full mirror of Java/Swift (recommended)
approaches.description: Add tree-sitter-php 0.25.2 to workspace and crate Cargo.toml and Cargo.lock; create languages/php.rs with ELEMENT_QUERY (function_definition, method_declaration, class, interface, trait, enum), CALL_QUERY (function_call_expression, member_call_expression, nullsafe_member_call_expression, scoped_call_expression), REFERENCE_QUERY (named_type), IMPORT_QUERY (namespace_use_declaration), DEFUSE_QUERY (assignment, augmented assignment, parameter, static, variable reads) and extract_inheritance walking base_clause and class_interface_clause children; register php in EXTENSION_MAP, supported_languages, mod.rs pub mod, get_language_info (LANGUAGE_PHP) and get_ts_language; add unit tests in php.rs and an integration test file under crates/aptu-coder/tests/ using common::call_tool_raw; add README entry.
pros: Matches the issue acceptance criteria and the five-constant handler contract exactly
Every capture name follows the contract consumed by parser_elements.rs, so DEFUSE, call graph and inheritance work without consumer changes
Swift and Java give direct, already-passing templates for tests and handler shape
All node kinds and fields were checked against php/src/node-types.json
cons: Needs care with the PHP-specific walk (base_clause and class_interface_clause are unnamed-field children, not field()s)
Adds about 8 files and a new grammar crate, with binary size delta to report
Dependency age gate: pin 0.25.1 or verify 0.25.2 publish date before merging

approaches.name: B: Minimal registration with DEFUSE_QUERY set to None
approaches.description: Same registry wiring as A, but php.rs contains only ELEMENT_QUERY, CALL_QUERY, IMPORT_QUERY and extract_inheritance, and the LanguageInfo entry sets defuse_query: None (as fortran and markdown do in mod.rs).
pros: Smallest handler; fewer compile-time query risks
Fortran, markdown and yaml already use defuse_query: None, so the pattern exists
cons: Fails the issue's explicit requirement that php.rs has the five query constants including DEFUSE_QUERY
Def-use analysis returns no sites for PHP files, a visible gap next to Java, Swift and C#
Leaves a follow-up issue for the same file

approaches.name: C: Derive queries from the grammar's tags.scm and remap captures
approaches.description: Start from tree-sitter-php queries/tags.scm (v0.25.2) for ELEMENT and CALL patterns, e.g. (class_interface_clause [(name) (qualified_name)] @name) and (scoped_call_expression name: (name) @name), then rename captures to aptu-coder's @function, @class, @call names and keep the same wiring as A.
pros: Reuses the grammar maintainers' own symbol patterns, which lowers the risk of missed node kinds
Easy to keep aligned with future grammar releases
Includes reference.implementation pattern for implements clauses
cons: tags.scm uses @definition.* and @reference.* capture names that must be remapped, so it is not a drop-in
Its patterns are tuned for tagging, not for the element-count and name-by-field contract, so each still needs checking
Does not reduce the amount of test work

recommendation: Approach A. It is the only option that satisfies the issue's acceptance criteria (five query constants including DEFUSE_QUERY, extract_inheritance, registry wiring for php in both lang.rs and languages/mod.rs, unit and integration tests). The Swift commit dbc2971 shows the exact file set. Use tree_sitter_php::LANGUAGE_PHP (not PHP_ONLY) so that the HTML-mixed edge case parses. Borrow the ELEMENT and CALL patterns from tags.scm (approach C) as a cross-check, and pin tree-sitter-php to 0.25.2 only after confirming its crates.io publish date is at least 7 days old, else use 0.25.1. Do not ship approach B, since DEFUSE_QUERY is an explicit requirement.

element_query_draft:
r"
(function_definition
  name: (name) @function_name) @function
(method_declaration
  name: (name) @method_name) @function
(class_declaration
  name: (name) @class_name) @class
(interface_declaration
  name: (name) @interface_name) @class
(trait_declaration
  name: (name) @trait_name) @class
(enum_declaration
  name: (name) @enum_name) @class
"

Node kinds and fields, each confirmed in php/src/node-types.json (v0.25.2): function_definition has field name (required, type name); method_declaration has field name (required, type name); class_declaration has field name (required, type name); interface_declaration has field name (required, type name); trait_declaration has field name (required, type name); enum_declaration has field name (required, type name). Captures: @function on function_definition and method_declaration (the name field is read in code via child_by_field_name("name")), @class on class, interface, trait and enum declarations.
defuse_query_draft:
r"
(assignment_expression left: (variable_name (name) @write.assign))
(augmented_assignment_expression left: (variable_name (name) @writeread.update))
(simple_parameter name: (variable_name (name) @write.param))
(static_variable_declaration name: (variable_name (name) @write.local))
(variable_name (name) @read.usage)
"

Adapted from java.rs DEFUSE_QUERY (verbatim, lines 33-36): (local_variable_declaration declarator: (variable_declarator name: (identifier) @write.local)) / (assignment_expression left: (identifier) @write.assign) / (update_expression (identifier) @writeread.update) / (identifier) @read.usage. PHP has no local declaration node with a declarator, so the local-declaration role is covered by static_variable_declaration (fields: name: variable_name, value: expression) and by parameters (simple_parameter field name: variable_name). Assignment uses left: variable_name (field confirmed in node-types.json assignment_expression fields left and right). Augmented assignment (+=, .=, ??= etc.) uses augmented_assignment_expression with field left: variable_name, and is captured as writeread. Reads are every variable_name whose name child is captured. Captures use the (name) child, not the whole variable_name, so the captured text equals the symbol without $ (parser_elements.rs 866-870 compares text to symbol_name). Java identifier patterns are not used because PHP has no identifier node kind (node-types.json lists no identifier type).
inheritance_walk_citation: Source: common/define-grammar.js of tree-sitter/tree-sitter-php at tag v0.25.2 (fetched with gh api). For a class declaration: class_declaration (define-grammar.js 365-373) is seq(optional(field('attributes', attribute_list)), repeat(_modifier), keyword('class'), field('name', reserved('classes', name)), optional(base_clause), optional(class_interface_clause), field('body', declaration_list)). The walk is: (1) start at the class_declaration node; (2) read its name with child_by_field_name("name") (node-types.json class_declaration fields: attributes, body, name); (3) there is NO field name for the extends or implements clauses, so iterate node.child(i) and match child.kind() == "base_clause" for extends and child.kind() == "class_interface_clause" for implements; (4) for base_clause, define-grammar.js 334-337 is seq(keyword('extends'), commaSep1($._name)), so the names are the NAMED children whose kind is name, qualified_name or relative_name (node-types.json base_clause children: name, qualified_name, relative_name); the keyword 'extends' is anonymous and is skipped by named_child iteration; (5) for class_interface_clause, define-grammar.js 381-384 is seq(keyword('implements'), commaSep1($._name)), with the same named-child kinds (node-types.json class_interface_clause children: name, qualified_name, relative_name); (6) emit format!("extends {text}") for each base_clause name and format!("implements {text}") for each class_interface_clause name, in source order; (7) return an empty Vec when neither child exists. Interfaces (define-grammar.js 326-330) use optional(base_clause) for extends lists and enum_declaration (339-344) uses optional(class_interface_clause) only, so the same walk covers them. The tags.scm reference pattern (class_interface_clause [(name) (qualified_name)] @name) confirms the named-child kinds.
